{
  "summary": "Add a tamper‑evident ledger that records every receipt and mileage operation, supports history views, export verification, and backup integrity checks. Implement ledger core (src/lib/ledger.ts) with append‑only encrypted storage, canonical JSON hashing (SHA‑256 via @noble/hashes), import of existing data on first launch, and verifyLedger routine. Extend receipt and mileage stores to push ledger entries on create, update, delete. Add UI screens for History (detail view) and ledger status in Settings. Update ui_flow.json to include the new navigation steps. Ensure backup and restore incorporate ledger verification, and older backups are imported as \"imported\" entries. All existing tests must keep passing; new unit and acceptance tests will cover hash chaining, detection of tampering, history correctness, import behavior, export verification, and backup validation.",
  "files": [
    "src/lib/ledger.ts",
    "src/lib/receiptStore.ts",
    "src/lib/mileageStore.ts",
    "src/lib/backup.ts",
    "src/screens/ReceiptDetailScreen.tsx",
    "src/screens/MileageDetailScreen.tsx",
    "src/screens/SettingsScreen.tsx",
    "src/components/ui/HistoryList.tsx",
    "ui_flow.json"
  ],
  "steps": [
    "1. Create src/lib/ledger.ts: define LedgerEntry type, constants, helper functions for canonical JSON (stable field order), hash calculation (import { sha256 } from '@noble/hashes/sha2.js', { bytesToHex, utf8ToBytes } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js'), appendEntry(entryWithoutHash) that computes hash, sets prevHash, seq, at (ISO string), stores entry encrypted via Store.append (new method to be added). Provide methods: initLedgerIfNeeded(store) – on first launch reads existing receipts and mileage entries and writes a single imported entry per record, with import date; addEntry(kind, recordId, data) used by stores; verifyLedger(store) – reads all entries, recomputes hashes, returns {ok, entries, firstBadSeq?, reason?}. Export needed functions.",
    "2. Extend src/lib/storage/store.ts (or create a small wrapper) with a new method appendLedgerEntry(entry: LedgerEntry): Promise<void> that reads existing ledger array (or empty), pushes new entry, writes back encrypted JSON. Ensure no overwriting of previous entries; only delete on full data reset.",
    "3. Update src/lib/receiptStore.ts: after any successful createReceipt, editReceipt, deleteReceipt, call ledger.addEntry with kind 'receipt.created', 'receipt.corrected', or 'receipt.deleted' respectively. Pass full record content after change (for deletion, pass the last known content). Include OCR pre‑fill and user‑confirmed data in the stored data object (e.g., { ...receipt, ocrData }). Ensure the store continues to use encrypted storage as before.",
    "4. Update src/lib/mileageStore.ts similarly: after addMileageEntry, editMileageEntry, deleteMileageEntry call ledger.addEntry with 'mileage.created', 'mileage.corrected', 'mileage.deleted'. Store full mileage record after change.",
    "5. Modify src/lib/backup.ts: when creating a backup, include the ledger array in the backup payload under key \"ledger\". When restoring, first call ledger.verifyLedger on the restored payload; if verification fails, throw an error with a friendly message (\"Backup verification failed – data may be tampered\"). If backup has no ledger (old version), after successful restore import each receipt/mileage as 'imported' ledger entries using ledger.addEntry with kind 'imported' and the import date set to now.",
    "6. Add UI components:",
    "   a. src/components/ui/HistoryList.tsx – a simple component that receives an array of LedgerEntry objects and renders them chronologically (newest last) showing at, kind, and a JSON preview of data.",
    "   b. src/screens/ReceiptDetailScreen.tsx – existing receipt detail/edit screen should receive a navigation param \"showHistory\" or have a button \"History\" that navigates to this screen, loads the ledger entries filtered by recordId = receipt.id, and displays HistoryList. Ensure the screen still allows editing the receipt.",
    "   c. src/screens/MileageDetailScreen.tsx – analogous to receipt detail, with a History button and HistoryList filtered by mileage.id.",
    "   d. src/screens/SettingsScreen.tsx – add a new section showing ledger verification status: call ledger.verifyLedger(store) on mount; display \"Verified • N entries • intact\" when ok, otherwise display a warning with the first bad seq and reason.",
    "7. Update ui_flow.json: add steps for opening a receipt’s History view from the receipt edit screen and for the Settings screen to display the ledger status text. Ensure the primary flow (edit receipt → open History → see correction) is represented.",
    "8. Add unit tests (will be added later by the test writer) for:",
    "   - canonical JSON ordering and hash generation.",
    "   - verifyLedger detecting a changed field, missing entry, reordered entry, and changed prevHash, reporting firstBadSeq.",
    "   - corrections keep original entry and add corrected entry.",
    "   - import runs only once on a fresh install.",
    "   - CSV export appends verification line and ledger entry; tampering the file makes verification fail.",
    "   - PDF export verification code matches ledger head hash; unknown codes are reported as not from this app.",
    "   - backup round‑trip keeps a verifying ledger; tampered backup is rejected.",
    "9. Ensure all existing tests continue to pass: do not modify existing receipt/mileage store signatures beyond adding async calls to ledger; keep existing validation, encryption, and UI flow unchanged.",
    "10. Run lint, TypeScript compile, and existing Jest tests to confirm no regressions."
  ],
  "has_ui": true
}

      "severity": "medium",
      "where": "code",
      "file": "src/lib/ledger.ts",
      "issue": "The ledger is stored as a single encrypted JSON array in the Store, and the appendLedgerEntry method reads the whole array, pushes a new entry, and writes it back. This could allow a maliciously‑crafted Store implementation (or a corrupted on‑device storage) to replace prior entries, breaking the append‑only guarantee. The code relies on the Store's internal security but does not enforce immutability at the ledger level.",
      "fix": "Make the ledger truly append‑only by storing each entry under its own key (e.g. \"ledger:{seq}\") and never reading‑modifying previous entries.     },
    {
      "id": "ledger-entry-size",
      "severity": "medium",
      "where": "deployment",
      "file": "src/lib/ledger.ts",
      "issue": "There is no explicit limit on the size of a ledger entry's data field. Very large receipt images or OCR data could cause the encrypted ledger blob to grow without bound, leading to storage exhaustion on the device or DoS during backup/restore.",
      "fix": "Enforce a reasonable maximum size for the data payload (e.g., reject entries > 256 KB) before calling addEntry, and document the limit. The backup routine should also cap total ledger size (e.g., 5 MiB) and abort with a user‑friendly error if exceeded."
    },
    {
      "id": "photo-uri-path-traversal",
      "severity": "medium",
      "where": "code",

      "fix": "Validate that any restored photoUri resolves within the app's documentDirectory (e.g., using FileSystem.getInfoAsync and checking the path prefix). Reject or sanitize any out‑of‑bounds paths before writing the file."

      "fix": "Replace the direct hash exposure with a HMAC keyed with a per‑device secret, or omit the head hash from the exported line and store it only in the ledger entry."
    },
    {
      "id": "missing-csp-web",
      "severity": "low",
      "where": "deployment",
      "file": "public/index.html",

# DEPLOYMENT.md

*This guide walks John (or any developer) from the current commit of **apps/freelance-finance-tracker** to a production‑ready iOS/Android release (with an optional static‑web fallback). All commands, file names, ports, and environment variables are taken from the repository; anything that does not yet exist is marked **TODO** and a stub is provided.*

---  

## What this app is

- **Type**: Mobile‑first, local‑first finance tracker built with **Expo SDK** (version taken from `package.json` via `npm view expo version`).  
- **Core story**: Users capture receipt photos, log mileage, view a dashboard and export tax‑ready CSV/PDF files. All data stays encrypted on‑device; there is no backend.  
- **New capabilities (v2.0)**  
  1. **Tamper‑evident ledger** – every create / edit / delete of a receipt or mileage entry appends an immutable, SHA‑256‑hashed ledger entry (`src/lib/ledger.ts`).  
  2. **History view** – a “History” screen shows the original entry and every correction, newest last.  
  3. **Export verification** – CSV/PDF exports end with a verification line and a ledger entry (`export.created`). Settings can verify an exported file.  
  4. **Backup hardening** – backups now include the ledger; restores run `verifyLedger` and abort on failure.  
- **Key files**  
  - Ledger core: `src/lib/ledger.ts` (defines `LedgerEntry`, `addEntry`, `verifyLedger`, import‑on‑first‑launch).  
  - Store extension: `src/lib/storage/store.ts` (new `appendLedgerEntry`).  
  - Receipt & mileage stores: `src/lib/receiptStore.ts`, `src/lib/mileageStore.ts` (call ledger on every mutation).  
  - UI components: `src/components/ui/HistoryList.tsx`, `src/screens/ReceiptDetailScreen.tsx`, `src/screens/MileageDetailScreen.tsx`, `src/screens/SettingsScreen.tsx`.  
  - Flow definition: `ui_flow.json` (updated with History navigation).  

---  

## Architecture

```
+-------------------+      +------------------------+      +-------------------+
|  React Native UI  | ---> |  Domain / Lib layer    | ---> |  Encrypted Store  |
| (Paper, Nav, FAB) |      | (pure‑logic only)      |      | (expo‑sqlite)     |
+-------------------+      +------------------------+      +-------------------+
        |                         |                              |
        v                         v                              v
   Expo runtime            src/lib/*.ts                expo-secure-store
   (iOS / Android)         (finance, receipt …)           (key)
```

- **UI layer** – screens in `src/screens/`, shared components in `src/components/ui/`.  
- **Domain layer** – pure functions (`src/lib/ledger.ts`, `src/lib/ocr.ts`, `src/lib/backup.ts`, …) fully unit‑testable.  
- **Storage layer** – `src/lib/storage/` abstracts encrypted SQLite (native) and a fallback for web (`device.web.ts`). Ledger entries are stored **append‑only** via `appendLedgerEntry`.  
- **Policy gate** – `src/screens/PolicyScreen.tsx` blocks all UI until `POLICY_VERSION` is accepted.  
- **No backend** – OTA updates via Expo Application Services (EAS).

## Security checklist

All items stem from the automated scan, the security review, and the production hardening work for this Expo app (including the new ledger). **Check each box after fixing the issue.**

### Dependency vulnerabilities (deployment actions)

- [ ] **`uuid`** – upgrade to `npm i uuid@^13.0.1` (fixes CVE‑2026‑141907).  
- [ ] **`node-forge`** – monitor for a fixed release (`>=1.5.0`) **or** replace with `@noble/*`. Ensure no import remains.  
- [ ] **`braces`** – monitor for `>=3.0.4` (CVE‑2026‑19387) or replace the glob utility.  
- [ ] **`sprintf-js`** – monitor for `>=1.1.2` (CVE‑2026‑97058) or replace with native template literals.  

### Ledger‑related hardening (new code)

- [ ] **Append‑only storage** – verify that `src/lib/storage/store.ts::appendLedgerEntry` only ever pushes to the stored array and never rewrites or deletes entries (except a full data reset).  
- [ ] **First entry `prevHash`** – confirm it is 64 zeroes (`"0".repeat(64)`).  
- [ ] **Canonical JSON** – ensure `src/lib/ledger.ts` uses a deterministic field order (e.g. `Object.keys(...).sort()`) before hashing.  
- [ ] **Hash calculation** – verify import of `sha256`, `bytesToHex`, `utf8ToBytes` from `@noble/hashes` and that `hash = bytesToHex(sha256(utf8ToBytes(canonicalJson)))`.  
- [ ] **Import on first launch** – `initLedgerIfNeeded` must run only once (store a flag, e.g. `ledgerInitialized` in the encrypted store).  
- [ ] **Export verification line** – CSV/PDF export code must append `entries | headHash | code` where `code` is first 12 hex chars of `sha256(exportContentWithoutLine)`.  
- [ ] **Export ledger entry** – `kind: "export.created"` must contain `{format, code, entries, headHash}`.  
- [ ] **Backup verification** – `src/lib/backup.ts` must call `verifyLedger` on the restored payload **before** mutating any data; abort with a user‑friendly error if verification fails.  
- [ ] **Legacy backup handling** – older backups without a ledger are imported as `"imported"` entries (already implemented).  

### Existing code findings (must be addressed)

- [ ] **Data‑reset photo leak (high)** – `src/lib/dataReset.ts` must enumerate every stored `photoUri` and delete those files via `expo-file-system` before clearing the store.  
- [ ] **Backup‑restore path traversal (medium)** – `src/lib/backup.ts` must validate that any restored image paths stay inside `FileSystem.documentDirectory`.  
- [ ] **Backup‑restore size DOS (medium)** – reject encrypted backup blobs > 10 MiB **before** decryption and enforce max 10 000 receipts / 5 000 mileage entries in `validateBackupStructure`.  
- [ ] **Backup‑passphrase brute‑force (medium)** – add exponential back‑off and lockout after 5 consecutive failures (store count in memory).  
- [ ] **CSV export injection (medium)** – replace custom CSV builder with `csv-stringify` to guarantee proper escaping.  
- [ ] **Backup temporary file cleanup (medium)** – ensure `src/lib/backup.ts` deletes temp files in a `finally` block (`FileSystem.deleteAsync(tmpUri, { idempotent: true })`).  

### Hardening items introduced in v1.0 (must be verified)

- [ ] **Numeric field validation** – `src/lib/validation.ts` used everywhere; error messages appear via `<HelperText type="error">`.  
- [ ] **Backup passphrase policy** – UI enforces “≥ 12 characters” rule and disables the “Create backup” button until satisfied.  
- [ ] **Export button throttling** – CSV/PDF export buttons disabled while an export runs (`exportRunning` state).  
- [ ] **Backup structure validation** – `src/lib/backup.ts` exposes `validateBackupStructure`; restores only after passing.  
- [ ] **Temporary backup file deletion** – confirmed via `finally` block.

## CI/CD

**GitHub Actions workflow (place at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`)**

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm test                 # all Jest tests, including ledger tests
      - run: npm run test:ledger      # optional extra sanity check
      - run: npm run test:backup

  build-ios:
    needs: test
    runs-on: macos-latest
    env:
      EAS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.EAS_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: expo/github-action@v8
        with:
          expo-version: latest
      - run: npm ci
      - run: eas login --token ${{ secrets.EAS_TOKEN }}
      - run: eas build --platform ios --profile production --non-interactive

  build-android:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      EAS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.EAS_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: expo/github-action@v8
        with:
          expo-version: latest
      - run: npm ci
      - run: eas login --token ${{ secrets.EAS_TOKEN }}
      - run: eas build --platform android --profile production --non-interactive

  publish:
    needs: [build-ios, build-android]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
      - name: Manual store submission reminder
        run: |
          echo "🚀 To submit, run the following commands (or automate them if credentials are stored in EAS Secret Manager):"
          echo "  eas submit --platform ios --latest --type archive"
          echo "  eas submit --platform android --latest --type apk"
```
